title: Invertibility of the pinned tensor-pullback counit along scheme isomorphisms
statement: Let $j:Y\to Z$ be an isomorphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with chosen derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. For any complex $M$ of structure-sheaf modules, the pinned homotopy-category counit $Lj^*Q_h(M)\to Q_h(j^*M)$ [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition] is invertible. No K-flatness or boundedness hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Derived pullback, composition; Tag 0DJ8 affine reduction; Tag 0098 stalk formula

proof.text: Since j is an isomorphism it is an open immersion. The tensor-pullback adjunction and the exact open-restriction adjunction have the same right adjoint, so left-adjoint uniqueness identifies tensor pullback with exact restriction.

Take a K-flat resolution P to M. Tensor pullback preserves its quasi-isomorphism by exactness. The derived-pullback computation makes its counit invertible at P, and left-derived uniqueness transfers this assertion to the pinned counit.
In the naturality square for P to M, the two localized vertical maps and the counit at P are invertible. Therefore the counit at M is invertible by cancellation.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of the counit-compatible affine spectrum transport
